principle: Gold is held in solution as the extremely stable aurocyanide complex Au(CN)2- (from potassium gold cyanide KAu(CN)2); at the cathode the complex is reduced Au(CN)2- + e- -> Au + 2CN-, depositing near-pure (24k) soft gold at 90-100% cathode current efficiency. Excess free cyanide (KCN) keeps the complex stable, dissolves drag-in contaminants, and prevents spontaneous immersion (displacement) deposition of gold onto less-noble metals, which is the root cause of poor adhesion in strike-less gold plating. The bath runs strongly alkaline (pH >10.5, typically 11-13) because at lower pH free cyanide converts to lethal HCN gas [FACT: published chemistry]. This is the historical and industrial reference chemistry against which all acid-hard-gold, neutral, sulfite and thiosulfate gold systems are benchmarked for stability, efficiency and deposit purity.

substrates: stainless steel via Wood's nickel strike
mild/spring steel via copper-strike + nickel underplate
zinc diecast via cyanide-copper strike + Ni
applicability.steel_wire_notes: Steel wire is NEVER plated with gold directly: iron displaces gold from solution (immersion deposit, zero adhesion) and iron dissolution poisons the bath. Canonical wire stack: degrease -> electroclean -> pickle -> (Wood's Ni strike if stainless / Cu or Ni strike if mild steel) -> sulfamate or Watts nickel underplate 2-5 um as diffusion barrier and pore blocker -> alkaline gold strike -> alkaline gold build [FACT: standard handbook practice]. Reel-to-reel continuous wire plating in cyanide gold is established industrial practice (connector/wire industry), so the owner's feed-through concept maps onto a solved wet-line problem rather than a vacuum-seal problem. High-strength/spring steel wire: cathodic hydrogen during cleaning/strike risks hydrogen embrittlement; post-plate bake 190-220 C for 4-24 h per ASTM B850-class practice [FACT: published practice].
applicability.non_conductive_notes: Electroplating requires a conductive surface; glass/ceramic houseware is out of scope unless first metallized (electroless Ni/Cu seed, silvering, or PVD seed layer) — see electroless/PVD process files. Metallic houseware (spoons, cups: stainless or brass) plates fine via the same strike logic, BUT cyanide-gold-plated surfaces for food contact need thickness >= ~1 um, pore-free deposit, and food-contact-migration verification; nickel underlayers are a known allergen/migration concern for cutlery [FACT: Ni sensitization is established; migration limits jurisdiction-specific — [UNKNOWN — needs local food-contact regulation check]].
applicability.jewelry_thickness_classes: flash/color gilding 0.05-0.175 um (decorative, months of wear life); 'gold electroplate' marking class >= 0.175 um; 'heavy gold electroplate' >= 2.5 um; micron plating 0.5-1.0 um (small-production jewelry sweet spot); vermeil = >= 2.5 um gold over sterling silver [FACT: published FTC/ISO-27874-class marking thresholds]. ASTM B488 (engineering) types by purity: Type I >=99.7% Au, Type II >=99.0, Type III >=99.9; alkaline cyanide bath naturally produces Type III soft gold, Code A hardness (<=90 HK25) [FACT: ASTM B488 class structure].

components.name: plating tank
components.purpose: hold electrolyte; chemically inert to hot alkaline cyanide
components.diy_notes: polypropylene or glass/PP beaker 1-10 L at bench scale; NEVER metal tanks (galvanic dissolution) [FACT: standard practice]

components.name: immersion heater + thermostat
components.purpose: hold 50-70 C; deposit quality and efficiency are temperature-sensitive
components.diy_notes: PTFE/quartz-sheathed aquarium-style or lab heater; +/-2 C control adequate

components.name: DC rectifier / power supply
components.purpose: constant-current source; gold thickness is charge-controlled (Faraday)
components.diy_notes: bench CC/CV supply 0-5 A, 0-12 V is ample; current control (not voltage) is the correct mode; ampere-minute counter or timer for thickness

components.name: insoluble anode
components.purpose: counter-electrode; gold is replenished as KAu(CN)2 salt, not from the anode
components.diy_notes: platinized titanium preferred; 316 stainless usable in alkaline cyanide (contributes trace Fe/Cr/Ni over time — accept at hobby scale); NEVER carbon in production (sheds particles) [FACT: platinized-Ti is the published standard insoluble anode]

components.name: cathode fixture (rack/wire guide)
components.purpose: electrical contact to work + positioning for uniform current distribution
components.diy_notes: for wire: copper or titanium contact wheel/clip above solution line; for continuous reel-to-reel: entry/exit sheaves, contact brushes OUT of solution, anode pairs flanking the wire runs

components.name: agitation
components.purpose: replenish Au+ at the cathode film; raises usable current density; prevents burning
components.diy_notes: magnetic stirrer or cathode-rod rocking; NEVER air sparging into a cyanide bath if it aerosolizes solution — mist is a cyanide exposure route [FACT: cyanide mist hazard]

components.name: gold strike cell (separate small tank)
components.purpose: dedicated low-metal strike bath so drag-in contamination and adhesion duty never load the expensive build bath
components.diy_notes: 0.5-2 L is enough; same heater/rectifier can be shared with a switch

components.name: rinse cascade + dedicated cyanide drag-out rinse
components.purpose: static drag-out rinse recovers gold and keeps cyanide out of the general drain; counterflow rinses after
components.diy_notes: 3 buckets: static drag-out (returns to bath as evaporation make-up), rinse 1, rinse 2; cyanide rinses must NEVER meet acid rinses — HCN [FACT: lethal-gas hazard]

components.name: ventilation + HCN monitoring
components.diy_notes: this is the component that makes true home-DIY unreasonable: cyanide rooms in industry mandate gas monitoring and antidote kits [FACT: published industrial-hygiene practice]

components.name: analysis kit
components.purpose: bath control: Au content, free KCN, carbonate, pH
components.diy_notes: pH meter, AgNO3 titration for free cyanide (itself a cyanide-handling task), gravimetric/XRF for Au; small shops often outsource analysis to the chemistry supplier

operation_sequence.action: verify workpiece finished the prep chain (see prep_chain_required) and carries an active nickel (or fresh gold-strike-ready) surface; water-break test
operation_sequence.parameters: unbroken water film over 100% of surface
operation_sequence.failure_watch: beading water = residual oil -> guaranteed adhesion failure; return to cleaning

operation_sequence.action: gold strike: live entry (current already on) into strike bath
operation_sequence.parameters: 1-3 A/dm2, 50-65 C, Au 1-2 g/L bath [FACT: published typical range]
operation_sequence.failure_watch: dead entry gives immersion gold = smutty, non-adherent film; strike layer should be uniform pale gold

operation_sequence.action: transfer to build bath without drying (rinse optional between strike and plate if chemistries match; both alkaline cyanide -> direct transfer acceptable)
plate in build bath under current control
operation_sequence.parameters: 0.1-0.5 A/dm2, 55-70 C, mild agitation [FACT: published typical range]; thickness by ampere-minutes: ~3-4 min per um at 0.5 A/dm2 assuming ~95-100% efficiency [FACT: Faraday calculation for Au(I), rho 19.3 g/cm3]
operation_sequence.duration: flash 1-3 min; 0.5 um ~ 5-15 min; 2.5 um ~ 25-60 min depending on CD
operation_sequence.failure_watch: brown/burnt matte edges = CD too high or Au depleted; gas streaks = too little agitation; dull overall = carbonate high or organic contamination

operation_sequence.action: withdraw over tank, drain-dwell to minimize drag-out
operation_sequence.parameters: 5-10 s drain, drip back to bath
operation_sequence.failure_watch: drag-out is the #1 gold loss route at small scale

operation_sequence.action: static drag-out rinse (cyanide-segregated), then 2-stage flowing rinse, then hot DI rinse
operation_sequence.parameters: final rinse 60-80 C DI for spot-free drying
operation_sequence.failure_watch: cyanide rinse water is hazardous waste until treated; never to acid drain

operation_sequence.action: dry (warm air) and, for high-strength steel wire, hydrogen-embrittlement relief bake
operation_sequence.parameters: bake 190-220 C, 4-24 h per ASTM B850-class schedule [FACT: published practice]; note soft gold tolerates this, hard golds soften >200 C
operation_sequence.failure_watch: skipping bake on spring-steel wire that will be formed = delayed brittle fracture

operation_sequence.action: bath bookkeeping: log ampere-minutes, replenish KAu(CN)2 per Ah, titrate free KCN weekly, check pH and carbonate
operation_sequence.parameters: replenish ~0.12 g Au per A·min at 100% CE (2 g Au per 1000 A·s equivalent) [ESTIMATE: handbook-range, high confidence — direct Faraday arithmetic]
operation_sequence.failure_watch: letting Au fall below ~50% of make-up = burning at normal CD; carbonate >90 g/L = dull deposits

prep_chain_required: 1. solvent or ultrasonic alkaline degrease — remove drawing lubricants/oils from steel wire; oil = adhesion failure at any later step
2. alkaline soak clean 60-80 C — bulk soil removal
3. cathodic then brief anodic electroclean (30-80 C, 3-8 A/dm2) — scrub via gas evolution, anodic finish avoids smut redeposition; on high-strength wire minimize cathodic time (hydrogen pickup)
4. rinse; water-break test — verification gate before acids
5. acid pickle: HCl 10-30 vol% (mild steel) — strip oxide/scale; NOTE: pickle rinses and cyanide rinses on segregated drains, mixing acid with cyanide anywhere makes HCN [FACT]

6. IF stainless steel: Wood's nickel strike (NiCl2 ~240 g/L + HCl ~120 mL/L, 3-10 A/dm2, 1-4 min, live entry) — breaks the passive Cr-oxide film; adhesion is impossible on passive stainless without it [FACT: published standard]
7. IF mild/carbon steel: copper strike (cyanide or alkaline non-cyanide copper) OR direct nickel strike — prevents immersion copper/gold displacement and seals the porous steel surface

8. nickel underplate 2-5 um (sulfamate for max ductility if the wire will be formed after plating; Watts bright for premium mirror look) — diffusion barrier (Fe->Au), pore-corrosion barrier, leveler; the single biggest wear-life lever under thin gold [FACT: standard practice]
9. rinse and transfer WET and LIVE into gold strike (step 2 of operation_sequence) — nickel repassivates in minutes; no drying anywhere between strike and gold

deposit_properties.purity_karat: 99.9%+ Au, 24 karat ('fine gold' color) from the pure build bath [FACT]; flash/color variants intentionally alloyed, effective karat of the coating 18-23k by recipe [ESTIMATE: handbook-range]
deposit_properties.hardness_HV: soft gold ~60-90 HK25 (roughly 60-90 HV at low load) [FACT: published typical range]; compare cobalt/nickel-hardened acid golds 130-200 HK25 — those belong to the acid-gold process file
deposit_properties.thickness_per_pass: practically 0.05-5 um in one continuous run; >5 um is possible (high efficiency) but slow and rarely economic for jewelry; thickness is linear in ampere-minutes
deposit_properties.color_control: pure bath gives the standard rich yellow 24k color, matte-to-satin without brighteners; brightness usually inherited from a bright nickel underplate ('bright nickel + thin gold' = premium look trick); hue variants via the flash bath alloy additions; color measured against reference plaques or by CIELAB in bigger shops
deposit_properties.ductility_forming_notes: CRITICAL ANSWER for plate-then-form: soft 24k alkaline-cyanide gold is the MOST ductile gold deposit available (several % elongation, fine equiaxed grain) and tolerates post-plate wire bending far better than hard acid golds, which crack on forming [FACT: published soft-vs-hard gold behavior]. The stack's weak link when bending plated steel wire is (a) the nickel underplate — choose low-stress sulfamate nickel, not bright Watts (brighteners embrittle it), and (b) adhesion at the strike interfaces. Small-radius bends (ring making, r < ~5x wire diameter) will still craze any real stack at micron thickness; the robust production order is FORM FIRST, THEN PLATE, using rack/barrel plating of formed rings — this chemistry supports that order cheaply, which is its practical answer to the owner's Q3 [ESTIMATE: handbook-range reasoning, high confidence]. Heat-assisted forming: keep below ~200 C and brief; soft gold itself tolerates it, but Au-Ni/Au-Cu interdiffusion above ~150-250 C over time causes color drift and adhesion-adjacent brittleness [ESTIMATE: handbook-range, medium confidence].

defects_and_remedies.defect: burnt, brown/matte rough deposit at edges/high-current points
defects_and_remedies.cause: current density too high for Au content/temperature/agitation; or Au depleted
defects_and_remedies.remedy: lower CD, raise temperature/agitation, analyze and replenish Au

defects_and_remedies.cause: passive nickel (delay/drying before gold strike), skipped strike, dead entry, oil residue
defects_and_remedies.remedy: re-activate, enforce wet live-entry transfer and water-break discipline; strip and replate

defects_and_remedies.defect: immersion (displacement) gold smut, no adhesion, on strike-less work
defects_and_remedies.cause: work entered gold bath currentless or free cyanide too low
defects_and_remedies.remedy: always live entry; use the strike; restore free KCN

defects_and_remedies.defect: dull, hazy deposit from a previously good bath
defects_and_remedies.cause: carbonate buildup (>~60-90 g/L) or organic contamination
defects_and_remedies.remedy: carbonate freeze-out or partial remake; carbon treatment for organics

defects_and_remedies.defect: dark/off-color deposit, red/brassy or gray tinge
defects_and_remedies.cause: metallic contamination (Cu, Pb, Fe from drag-in or attacked fixtures)
defects_and_remedies.remedy: dummy-plate at low CD onto corrugated cathode; fix the drag-in source; strengthen strike as sacrificial buffer

defects_and_remedies.cause: contact-wheel arcing, wire vibration touching anode shields, gas streaking
defects_and_remedies.remedy: clean contacts above solution, guide alignment, raise agitation, lower CD

defects_and_remedies.defect: gold coating cracks when the wire is formed into rings
defects_and_remedies.cause: hard/bright nickel underplate embrittlement, excessive gold thickness on small bend radius, or hydrogen embrittlement of the steel
defects_and_remedies.remedy: switch to sulfamate nickel, plate thinner then flash after forming, or invert the flow: form first, plate formed rings; bake per B850 for high-strength wire
rinse fixtures back into bath (gold recovery), control level with drag-out-rinse returns

defects_and_remedies.cause: low temperature, low Au, high free cyanide beyond range
defects_and_remedies.remedy: restore operating window by analysis, not guesswork

cost_drivers: gold metal itself dominates: bath inventory (e.g. 5 L at 10 g/L Au = 50 g Au locked in solution before the first part is plated) plus per-part gold at ~0.019 g per cm2 per um [FACT: density arithmetic]
drag-out losses — at small scale often exceed deposited gold unless a static drag-out rinse returns solution to the bath
KAu(CN)2 salt price carries a fabrication premium over spot gold (~5-15% typical) [ESTIMATE: handbook-range, low-medium confidence — market dependent]

cyanide compliance: licensed purchase of KCN/KAu(CN)2, storage security, HCN monitoring, antidote kit, operator training — a fixed overhead that dwarfs chemistry cost at DIY scale [FACT: these obligations exist; exact local licensing [UNKNOWN — jurisdiction specific]]
waste treatment: alkaline-chlorination cyanide destruction or licensed hauler for every dump and rinse stream
nickel underplate line (its own tanks, chemistry, control) — required for quality on steel, roughly doubles the wet line
analysis: titrations/XRF or supplier lab service per week of operation
insoluble platinized-Ti anodes: high first cost, long life
energy is negligible (low voltage, high efficiency) — labor and gold accounting are the real variable costs

hazards: KCN and KAu(CN)2 are acutely lethal by ingestion, skin absorption and inhalation (GHS acute toxicity cat. 1/2; H300/H310/H330) [FACT]
contact of any cyanide solution/salt/rinse with ANY acid releases hydrogen cyanide gas — rapidly fatal; this includes accidental drain mixing with pickle acids (EUH032) [FACT]
bath pH falling below ~10.5 begins HCN evolution even without gross acid addition [FACT]
hot 55-70 C strongly alkaline (KOH, corrosive H314) solution — splash/burn hazard [FACT]
cyanide mist from agitation/gassing is an inhalation route [FACT]
nickel compounds in the prep chain: carcinogen category and skin-sensitizer classes [FACT]
classic grain refiners (thallium, arsenic compounds) if present: highly toxic / carcinogenic classes [FACT]
environmental: cyanides and nickel acutely toxic to aquatic life (H410); illegal to drain untreated [FACT]
controls: engineering: dedicated ventilated area or fume extraction over tanks; HCN gas monitor with alarm; physically separated and labeled acid vs cyanide zones, separate drains, separate spill kits
chemical: keep every cyanide bath and rinse alkaline (pH >10.5) at all times; pH-adjust only with dilute KOH, never any acid near the bath
PPE: nitrile/butyl gloves, face shield, apron; no lone working with cyanide; cyanide antidote kit (per local medical guidance) and emergency plan on site [FACT: industrial mandate class]
storage: cyanide salts locked, dry, ventilated, far from acids and oxidizers; purchase and holding per local poisons/precursor licensing [UNKNOWN — jurisdiction specific]
procedure: written SOP, ampere-minute and chemical logs, no eating/drinking, decontamination rinse discipline
safety.waste: spent baths and cyanide-bearing rinses: gold first recovered (electrowinning/dummy plating or supplier refining credit), then cyanide destroyed by alkaline chlorination (NaOCl at pH >10.5, verify CN- below discharge limit) or shipped to a licensed hazardous-waste processor; NEVER acidify, NEVER sewer untreated; nickel-bearing prep wastes handled as heavy-metal waste [FACT: standard treatment route]

diy_feasibility.verdict: NOT RECOMMENDED for home/DIY despite being technically the simplest and best-documented gold chemistry. The electrochemistry would run happily in a 2 L beaker with a $50 power supply; the cyanide is what disqualifies it. For the owner's DIY-to-small-production goal, this process is the REFERENCE to understand and the benchmark to compare against, while actual small-scale work should start on cyanide-free (sulfite/thiosulfate) or purchased ready-made low-free-cyanide pen/bath solutions handled as sealed products — see the sibling process files.
diy_feasibility.minimum_viable_setup: IF operated anyway as a licensed micro-shop (not a home): ~2-10 L PP tanks x (electroclean, pickle [separate room/zone], Ni strike, Ni plate, Au strike, Au build, drag-out + rinses), 2 bench rectifiers, heaters, platinized-Ti anodes, pH meter + AgNO3 titration kit, fume extraction + HCN monitor, locked chemical storage, cyanide destruction reagents (NaOCl, KOH), documented SOPs. Realistic minimum ~USD 3-8k hardware + gold inventory + licensing, before any part is sold [ESTIMATE: component-sum, medium confidence]
diy_feasibility.hard_limits: KCN/KAu(CN)2 purchase is licence-gated in most jurisdictions (exact regime [UNKNOWN — jurisdiction specific]); no safe way to run free-cyanide chemistry without ventilation + monitoring + a second trained person; waste cannot be legally self-disposed without a treatment step; insurers/landlords typically exclude cyanide operations in residential premises; none of these limits soften with skill — they are fixed regulatory/toxicological floors
